title: A claim has to be able to fail a check
pattern: State the claim, name an observation that would show it is wrong, and go look.
novel_use: Use this when a large story is standing in for a measurement.
guardrail: If nothing could prove the claim false, do not call it science.

support.source: Cargo Cult Science, Caltech commencement address, 1974
support.note: A scientific claim has to name a check that could show it is wrong.

title: An analogy, and where it breaks
pattern: Give an ordinary object, say which quantity it stands for, then say the step where the likeness stops.
novel_use: This is how a hard idea becomes something you can hold, and then put down.
guardrail: The analogy is not the law. The place it breaks is part of the explanation.

support.source: The Character of Physical Law; The Feynman Lectures on Physics
support.note: An everyday picture is followed by the step where the picture stops holding.

title: Doubt the authority, check the evidence
pattern: Restate the official conclusion, ask how the evidence was made, and look for one observation that would separate two explanations.
novel_use: Authority is a hint about where to look, not a reason to stop.
guardrail: Doubt without a check is not science.

support.source: Cargo Cult Science, 1974; What is Science?, 1966 address to the National Science Teachers Association
support.note: Science is rechecking by new experience, not a belief that the expert is done.

title: A joke, then the calculation
pattern: A concrete joke can get someone to look. Then do the calculation.
novel_use: The joke is how you get to the picture. It is not the result.
guardrail: Do not let the joke replace the number or the check.

support.source: Surely You're Joking, Mr. Feynman!; The Feynman Lectures on Physics
support.note: A concrete joke can open a picture. The lectures then go back to the equation.

title: What was seen, what was inferred, what was guessed
pattern: Separate what was seen, what you infer from it, and what you are only guessing.
novel_use: Say which of the three a sentence is before you build on it.
guardrail: A guess has to be labeled as a guess.

support.note: Scientific integrity means you report what might make the claim wrong, not only the favorable bits.
